chains.name: Ethereum

chains.exposure: All historical public keys visible on-chain

chains.name: Bitcoin
chains.detail: BIP-360 (P2MR, Pay-to-Merkle-Root — Taproot without the key-path spend; formerly P2QRH) merged as a draft Feb 2026; no activation plan or date. BIP-361 (Lopp et al., legacy-signature sunset/freeze) is a draft. Hash-based address types (P2PKH/P2WPKH) protect unspent outputs until first spend; Taproot (P2TR) outputs expose the key on-chain. Oct 2026: Justin Drake's 'bunker mode' call urges migrating exposed-key funds to fresh hash-protected addresses. Oct 13 2026: Coinbase (custodian of ~5% of BTC) published recommendations, framed as 'input to an open discussion' — start now, P2MR/P2TRv2 output containers, a staged 1-of-2 hybrid (classical or PQ key) spend path, a stateless PQ option, MPC-friendly schemes for custodians; dormant-coin policy handled separately, no position taken.
chains.exposure: ~6-6.9M BTC (~31% of supply) behind exposed public keys — reused addresses, spent-from addresses, P2PK, and Taproot (CoinDesk, Europol, Oct 2026)
watch: Coinbase's 1-of-2 hybrid spend path appears in a BIP or Bitcoin Core PR
A PQ signature BIP (e.g. SHRINCS) selects an MPC-compatible scheme custodians can run
Coinbase or ETF sponsors publish a dated custody-key migration plan
